title: Practice: describing transformations
intro: Ten questions. Type a column vector as two numbers, top then bottom.

questions.prompt: Match each transformation to the information needed to describe it fully.

right.text: The equation of the mirror line

questions.explanation: Missing any one of these loses marks — for example, a rotation without its centre is not fully described.

questions.prompt: Each point is reflected onto its image. Give the equation of the mirror line.
hints: The mirror line passes through the midpoint and is perpendicular to the line joining the points.
questions.explanation: Midpoints: $y = 4$, $x = 2$, $y = 1.5$, and for the last pair the coordinates swap, so $y = x$.

questions.prompt: A(1, 2), B(2, 4), C(4, 3), D(5, 1) becomes A′(4, −2), B′(5, 0), C′(7, −1), D′(8, −3). Give the translation vector.
questions.explanation: Every point moves 3 right and 4 down: $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$.

questions.prompt: Triangle X(2, 3), Y(5, 4), Z(6, 1) becomes X′(−3, −2), Y′(−4, −5), Z′(−1, −6). What is the mirror line?
A(2, 1), B(4, 0), C(6, 2) becomes A′(7, 1), B′(9, 0), C′(11, 2). Describe the transformation.
hints: Has every point moved by the same amount?
questions.explanation: Every $x$ increases by 5 and $y$ stays the same, and the shape is not flipped — a translation.

hints: Does each one say everything needed?
questions.explanation: b has no direction, d has no centre. $180^\circ$ needs no direction, so e is complete.

questions.prompt: A(1, 2), B(4, 1), C(1, 5) becomes A′(−9, −2), B′(0, −5), C′(−9, 7). It is an enlargement. Give its scale factor and centre.
hints: Solve $-9 - a = 3(1 - a)$ for the centre's $x$.

questions.prompt: Point $(5, 6)$ is rotated $180^\circ$ about the origin. What is the $x$-coordinate of its image?
questions.explanation: A $180^\circ$ rotation about the origin maps $(x, y)$ to $(-x, -y)$: $(-5, -6)$.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for finding a centre of rotation in order.

items.text: Join A to its image A′ and B to its image B′
Construct the perpendicular bisectors of AA′ and BB′
Mark where the bisectors cross: this is the centre C
Measure the angle ACA′ to find the angle of rotation

questions.explanation: The centre is the same distance from a point and its image, so it lies on every perpendicular bisector.

questions.prompt: A rotation of $90^\circ$ clockwise is the same as a rotation of $270^\circ$ anticlockwise about the same centre.
questions.explanation: True — both end in the same position.
